links.reason: 1349 shows only a leap and a shot (வாளி சிந்தினான்); no wound, no laugh and no fall appears in the Tamil, so the 'pierced body falling' is imported from 1350. Kural 774 turns on மெய்வேல் பறியா நகும், a laughing pull at a spear in the body, which this verse never shows.
links.text_issue: Sense flagged uncertain; the fall the note relies on is in 1350, outside the unit.

links.reason: Both use a fruit-heavy tree (பழுமரப் பறவை / பயன்மரம் ... பழுத்தற்று), but 828 only likens a wedding crowd to birds; nothing says the house's wealth is held for others. The two-way giving rests on 829 and 831, which are not in the unit.

1495 says the couple enjoy வினைநலம் (the good fruit of deeds); 408 has the teacher go பழவினை பரிய நோற்பான் (wear away old deeds). The Jain link is real, but 408's old deeds are the ones that broke his penance, and neither verse says that enjoyed good karma is the same store penance wears away; that is the note's reading.

2060 says heaven's wealth ends (ஒருநாள் ஈறுடைய). TM 184 says even விண்ணுறுவாரையும் வினையுறுவாரையும் are cut at the counted thirty, a verse the marker cannot read; it speaks of death or age, not of heaven ending. The spans of seas and the way above by austerity are said to come from 2061-2063, outside the unit.

497 does follow Kural 759 (செய்க பொருள் ... செறுவாரைச் செறுகிற்கு எஃகு பிறிது இல்லை), though it is a paraphrase and not an echo. The irony of the later wreck is the note's own; the wreck was a staged trick (see 574, சீதத்தன் told it was வஞ்சம்), so it is not 'forces no amount of wealth can subdue'.

Both make கூற்றம் the outcome of unequal harm, with matching words: ஆற்றாது ... கண்ணீர் ... கூற்றமாய் வீழ்ந்துவிடும் against ஆற்றுவார்க்கு ஆற்றாதார் இன்னா செயல் ... கூற்றத்தைக் கையால் விளித்தற்றால். The pair gives the same law from both ends, strong harming weak and weak harming strong, which neither shows alone.

The world's cry எத்துணைத் தவஞ்செய் தான்கொல் echoes Kural 70's என்நோற்றான் கொல் in other words, but it is said of the one given the feast (வித்திய புகழினாற்கு), not of a father. The queen's title to the nurse (தாய்க்குச் சித்திரத் தேவிப் பட்டம்) is true of the verse, but the pairing is loose.
links.text_issue: Sense flagged uncertain; recipient of the feast unnamed.

links.reason: These are one episode told twice: 1237 (narrator) says he relieved the elephants' distress (பரிவு தீர்த்தான்), 1753 says rain poured as he stood grieving (சிந்தித்துக் கவன்று நிற்பத் திருமழை பொழிந்தது). The second tells how the first was done; it is not a rival credit, and 'he does not claim it' is nowhere in the Tamil.

The only tie is the name அசோகன்; 284 says an Asokan reached a divine world by earlier penance (தவத்தினின் அசோகன் ... அமருலகம்), and nothing in the Tamil fixes him as the king who reasons in 82. The marker itself says same name is not shown to be same person.

3020 praises the Jina whose word those who say it will not suffer (பரியாரே); TM 105 only says the Lord stands beyond இருவினை. Neither makes a claim about who removes deeds, and the 'whether a liberated one also helps' point is in neither verse. The tension is invented.
links.text_issue: Sense flagged uncertain; line 4 is repeated in 3021.

links.reason: 303 offers the queen alone among skulls as visible proof (காட்டுவாள் போல ... கண்டு இனித் தெளிக) for those who know sin only by hearsay (உரையில் கேட்பார்), and Kural 37 likewise says look and do not be told (வேண்டா ... சிவிகை பொறுத்தானோடு ஊர்ந்தான்). The epic adds the one-life reversal from விண்தொட நிவந்த கோயில் to the skull ground, a case the couplet's two persons do not give.

Both name the Lord of the pindi tree (பிண்டி நாதன் / முக்குடை ... பிண்டி மூர்த்தி), and 3051 follows 2844 in the sermon, so this is plot sequence. The kings leave their retinues out of longing for bliss (வேட்கையானே); nothing says this is a cost of following him.

1931 has the wardens tell the sufferers to take the fruit of earlier deeds (முன்னதிற் செய்த வினையின் முறை), but gives no reaction of the sufferers; Naladiyar 33's fool sighing and the wise saying தொல்லையது is therefore not shown in the pit. The pairing is the shared theme of வினைப்பயன்.

Both use the thorn for an enemy (முள்ளினால் முட்களையுமாறு; இளைதாக முள்மரம் கொல்க), but 879 never names an enemy and PN 308 is about setting the foe's inner foe against him. Timing against means is a real contrast, but a thin one.

The fenced crop is a real shared figure: சீல வேலி against பிணி செய் பன்மா, and சாந்த வேலி against the five cattle (பட்டி அஞ்சு). But 'a Jain version where no grace ripens' is the note's own; 379 names a crop ripening in age (கிழவு விளைக்கும் பைங்கூழ்) and says nothing of grace.

The lists overlap only in anger (குரோதன் / வெகுளி); Kural 360 has காமம், வெகுளி, மயக்கம், the verse has anger, pride, deceit, greed. It is a different list, not a widening, and nothing ties the Kural to a school. 3080 shows the passions slain, not their 'names perishing'.

Both are Jain-leaning grounds for renunciation (இளமை நீங்க மூப்பு; இளமை ... நிலையாமை), so the pair is the shared theme. 2799 is the opening of a sermon whose conclusion comes later in the same chapter, so 'the epic leaves it unsaid' is not shown; the quatrain is itself Jain, so it gains no 'Jain account' from the epic.

304 names father, mother, son and daughter who have turned in the stream of births (மாற்றிடைச் சுழன்ற பெற்றி); Naladiyar 15 is a chain of mothers (தாய்த்தாய்). Chain against exchange of roles is a true contrast, but 'grief for kin has no fixed object' is the note's gloss.

73 carries out an order to settle him outside the great city (மாநகர்ப் புறத்தினின் நன்னகர் சமைத்து), and 65 says நந்நகர்ப் புறத்தனைய னாடனீங்க (play outside), so it is fulfilment in plot order. 65 is not a sentence of exile and its sense is uncertain, so 'never takes effect as a punishment' is not shown.
links.text_issue: 65 flagged uncertain; addressee and son unclear.

links.reason: Kural 756's தெறுபொருள் is wealth got by crushing foes (ஒன்னாரைத் தெறு), but 665 is a demand on a king not yet crushed (வேண்டும்; வெண்குடை ஆய்தரல்). Applying it to a letter-demand stretches the couplet, and the Kural makes no claim the envoys could use to make the demand lawful.

1815 says the women who reached his chest தவஞ்செய்தாரே (did austerity before). Naladiyar 31's line மேலைத் தவத்தால் தவம்செய்யா தார் can be read either way (Pope's main text reads lack of former penance as the cause), so 'present comfort runs out' is one reading. The herald's praise is a conceit, not doctrine.

The note says 'as the verse says men leave the ripe jackfruit for the thorny date'; yasodhara 116 has no such image. It says only that the queen went to the keeper, கனிபுரை கிளவி (words sweet as fruit), cold to the king. The jackfruit and date are TM 201's alone.

885 is the maid's appeal to the city's praise (மாநகர் மாந்தர்கள் யாவரும் ... புகழ்ந்தார்); Kural 423 (எப்பொருள் யார்யார்வாய்க் கேட்பினும்) fits against her argument. But 885 never shows the many to be wrong and the test both sides accept is in later verses, not in this unit.

1330 repeats 1329's opening (மலைமேலும் நின்னை மதியாது வாழ்வன்) and answers it (சலமே உரைத்தி இதுவோ உன் ஆண்மை), so it is an adjacent reply, not an image. The repetition is real, but the teaching is only that a taunt is returned.

Yas 1 praises the omniscient lord's feet so that release be taught (வெவ்வினை விலகி வீடு விளப்பதற்கு); it makes no claim about who burns deeds. TM 117's sunstone burns the cotton only in the sun's presence, so grace against effort is a defensible clash, but yas 1 does not state the Jain side.

Both make the southern breeze spring's envoy (தென்றல் விடுதூதா ... வேனிலாற்கு விருந்தேந்தி; இளங்கால் தூதன் இசைத்தனன்) with spring as a king. It is a shared convention, true as told, but the difference of ends is slight.

553 has a vidyadhara say living alone is the worst misery (தனியவராகி வாழ்தல் சாதுயர்), which is persuasion for marriage. 28 shows brother, friends and wives renouncing together (புலம் துறப்ப), which is not lone living, so the clash is only about pleasure as a final value.

212 shows only the queen eating the cooked flesh and others calling it a trick (வயிற்றை வளர்தனள் ... மாயை செய்தனள்); that it is her victim's flesh is from other verses, as the note's own 'possibly' admits. The unit states no rule about compassion.

Both set the flood of desire against shame: நாண்வேலி உந்திக் கடலென எழுந்த வேட்கை and காமக் கடும்புனல் உய்க்கும் நாணொடு நல்லாண்மை என்னும் புணை. Raft against fence round நிறை is a true contrast, but the pair is a shared image and does not limit the couplet.

821 says the Tirthan's feet remove all sin done (செய்த ... பாவம் எல்லாம் தீர்த்திடும் தீர்த்தன்) and Kural 5 says இருவினையும் சேரா; the narrower claim against the wider is real. But the verse does not make the worship an expiation for killing, and the 'occasion of war' is not in the Tamil.

The kings' mockery (மணிப் பன்றி அற்று மறியுமோ) is answered by the shot that breaks boar and machine together (பன்றியியற்றரும் பொறியும் அற்று ... ஒருங்குடன் உதிர). That is irony fulfilled, not incompatible claims. 2204 does not show the kings' ruin, so the 'fire' lands only in later verses.

443-446 show a king who gives to both முறைவேண்டுநர் and குறைவேண்டுநர் with discerning sight (இடைத்தெரிந்து உணரும்), which suits Kural 548's easy access and judgment. But it only illustrates the rule and limits it nowhere.

The only tie is waking (நனவு / விழிப்பது). In 1216 it is waking from a lover's dream; in 339 birth is like waking after death-sleep. The note itself says nothing in the verse speaks of rebirth, so the pairing is built on one word.

1993 promises a return (போதர்வேன் ... எறிந்த கோல்) and 1504 shows a silent exit (புறக்கணித்து எழுந்து போகி). Two partings from different wives are not incompatible claims, and 1993 does not show how it ends.

In Manimekalai the king goes to circle Manipallavam for a month (ஒரு மதி எல்லை காத்தல் நின் கடன்), and the minister's objection (மன் உயிர் முதல்வன் அறமும் ஈது அன்று) is overruled, since the king gets to see his birth (என் பிறப்பு அறிந்தேன்). This is not a renunciation of the throne, and the epic does not weigh it the way the note says.
links.text_issue: Unit begins mid-sentence (line 115 continues the minister's speech from before the cut).

links.reason: 1113 puts கலவியும் களிப்பும் காமப் புலவியும் in one daze, and Kural 1109 has ஊடல் உணர்தல் புணர்தல் as love's gain. The epic agrees that the sulk is a pleasure; the 'blends what the couplet sequences' is the note's contrast, not a qualification.

308 has Udayanan weary of pleasure he thinks the fruit of செய்த தவம் and going to Vamana's feet; cc 27 has Civakan hear அறம் and renounce at the feet of அறிவன். Both go to a teacher, so the contrast of reflection and sermon is small and does not generalise to how the epics motivate renunciation.

1380 mocks a man with drawn sword who flees from one man (ஒருவனை ஒருவன் அஞ்சி ஓடுமேல்); Kural 775 is about the glare giving way at a thrown spear. Both belittle cowardice, but different cases do not set 'lines of disgrace', and the Vidyadharas' earlier shame is not shown.

Kural 505 says deeds are the touchstone of persons (கருமமே கட்டளைக் கல்); 894 tests a perfumed powder by the bees. Proof by effect is a shared theme; that the test works only if agreed beforehand rests on 890-891, outside the unit.

978 has death thought better than life at a woman's peril (பெண்ணுயிர் அவலம் நோக்கி ... வாழ்வின் சாதல்); the verse never says மானம், the honour Kural 969 is about. Reading honour into a rescue is the note's step, so the 'moved honour-death' is a theme dressed as a limit.

511 has சீதத்தன் tell the crew the suffering is வினையது விளைவு, and 574 has the vidyadhara declare the wreck was வஞ்சம். The doctrinal reading is thus set beside a human cause shown after, which the first verse alone does not give.

Both use the full moon in eclipse: kings are the moon caught by the serpent (மாசுணம் அடையப்பட்ட நிறைமதி), Civakan the moon freed (கோள்வாய் மதிய நெடியான் விடுத்தாங்கு). The pairing is clear, but 'marks him as winner' is the note's guess, and 454 is flagged uncertain.

2111 shuts the five gates (பொறியெனும் வாயில் ஐந்து) and posts guards; Naladiyar 59 has the five senses as ஐவாய guarded for release. Both guard the gates, so the link is real, but what the walls and twelve guards stand for is unstated, so 'part of a larger war' is a guess.
